sample.fixture: actual kernel FUSE; indexed synthetic metadata; no cloud account

scope_and_limits: Actual temporary Linux FUSE mount with 500000 generated indexed files in one directory, no cloud credentials or content reads.
The measured phase runs 16 different metadata lookups spanning the first through last filename, then one absent name. Index construction and final shutdown are outside that phase.

Name indexes restrict both arms of the normal metadata visibility query. Stale matching observations and duplicate names can add SQL work; this is not a guarantee for arbitrary invalid provider metadata.
Logical mount views are at most18 after the lookups and return to the root after normal invalidation/reclamation. No directory snapshot reservation is created.
RSS/PSS samples are process measurements, not total system/kernel page-cache usage. The high-water mark already includes initial metadata indexing.

This does not measure full directory enumeration, cold provider listing publication, writable local overlays, file contents, desktop thumbnails, many accounts, real Graph latency or long-session churn.
A separate Cargo target directory was used for this checkout to avoid reusing another worktree's incremental executable. Expected nonzero test execution was verified.
